quote: “The best way to begin a day well is to think, on awakening, whether we cannot give pleasure during the day to at least one person.”
source: Friedrich Nietzsche, Human, All-Too-Human, vol. I, section 589, The Day’s First Thought (trans. Helen Zimmern, 1909)

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg 51935, Helen Zimmern’s translation of Human, All-Too-Human, Part I (T. N. Foulis, Edinburgh and London, 1909), Ninth Division, aphorism 589
evidence.edition: T. N. Foulis, 1909 (Complete Works, ed. Oscar Levy)
evidence.locator: vol. I, section 589, The Day’s First Thought

reason: Aphorism 589 in Zimmern’s 1909 text reads exactly this as its first sentence; the second sentence, on prayer, is left off and nothing is altered. Not shipped, not at cap, not banned.
